0. FOREWORD

FOR COTS

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 February 1978, after the draft finalized by the Furniture Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 The fast changing developments and innovations in decigns have brought new concepts in designing furniture, where shortage of living space is efftx~ively solved by such furniture itemr having fplding arrwqcmwt so that thcsc could he stored in foldin g conditio;) while not in use. `TIP popularity of folding cot further increases due to the fact that large quantities of such cots can be stored and transported with compa:ntivt, ease. 0.3 This standard contains clause supply certain tcchnicsl information 9.1 which requires the purchaser at the time of placing orders. Id

0.4 I:or the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated cxpressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-196OC. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4, MANUFACTURE 4.1 Frame -

The frame for folding cots shall be made from steel tubular pipes of wall thickness not less than 2 mm and 25 mm as outside diameter or from mild steel angles of 40 x 40 x 3 mm section or from mild steel unequal channel section as in Fig. 2. The frame shall not have more than two joints. In case of tubular pipe frame a piece of pipe shall be inserted in the joint with outer diameter equal to inside diameter of the tubular frame and then the joint shall be secured by welding. The inside radius at bends shall not be more than 150 mm and the tube shall be bent without causing any cracks, uneveness or other defects in the bend. A hole of 10 mm diameter shall be provided at the centre of each bend for fixing mosquito curtain frame. _____ *Sp&ificationfor cold rolled carbon steel sheets ( second reuirion).

4.2 Legs - Legs shall be made from steel tubular pipe of not less than l-25 mm in thickness and 25 mm outside diameter or from mild steel For strength and rigidity the legs on angles of 40 x 40 x 4 mm section. each side shall be cross connected with tubular pipe of not less than 1.2 mm in thickness and 15 mm outside diameter or mild steel angle of The legs may be fitted with spring clamps for 40 x 40 x 4 mm section. holdings the legs with frame in the folded position when not in use. The free end of the legs shall be fitted with replaceable shoes made of good quality plastic or rubber. 4.3 NEWAR used for knitting of folding cots shall not be less than in width and'shall conform to IS : 1895-1970;. 5. plate 7.1 Scratch Hardness Test -A sample of mild steel 150 x 50 mm in size and thickness 0.3 15 mm finished as given in 6 shall be subjected to scratch hardness test in accordance with 15.1 of IS : lOl1964t1_. A scratch, showing the bare metal, shall not be produced on the test sample. 7.2 Pressure Test -Samples prepared from mild steel plates of thickness 0.315 mm and finished as given in 6 shall be subjected to pressure test in accordance with 15.2 of IS : lOl-1964-)t. The metal surface shall not be rendered visible when the test pieces are separated after the test. 7.3 Flexibility and Adhesion Test-A sample of mild steel plate 150 x 50 mm in size and thickness O-315 mm finished, as given in 6 shall be subjected to flexibility and adhesion test in accordance with 16 of IS : lOl-1964tt. The paint film on the' test piece shall not show damage, detachment or cracking when examined under x 10 magnification.

9.1 The purchaser shall supply the following information to the supplier along with the order: a) Whether spring clamps are required or not; b) Whether NEWAR is required or not; c) Where alternative methods of construction and finish are specified they shall be clearly stated in the order; and d) Whether frame and legs should be of tubes, angle or channel sections or a combination of the sections.
